85:1: Abu Jaafar, may God have mercy on him, said: His statement, And the heaven with the mansions, God Almighty swore by the heaven with the mansions. The commentators differed on the meaning of the towers in this place. Some of them said: What is meant by that is: the sky with its palaces. They said: The towers are the palaces. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And the sky with the constellations. Ibn Abbas said: Palaces in the sky. Someone else said: Rather, they are the stars. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, The constellations, that they claim that they are palaces in the sky, and it is said that they are the planets. Others said: What he meant by that is: the sky with its stars. They said: its stars: its constellations. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, Of the constellations, he said: The constellations are the stars. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh: And the sky with its constellations. He said: The stars. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And the heaven with its constellations, and its constellations are its stars. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: The sky is full of sand and water. Who said that? Al-Hasan bin Qaz’ah told me: He said: Husayn bin Numayr told us, on the authority of Sufyan bin Husayn, regarding his statement, And the sky with its constellations, he said: with sand and water. The first and most correct of the sayings about this is to say: The meaning of this is: And the sky has the mansions of the sun and the moon. This is because the zodiac sign is the plural of zodiac sign, and they are mansions that are high above the earth, and from that is the saying of God, And if you were in lofty towers (An-Nisa’: 78). They are mansions high in the sky, and they are twelve mansions, so the moon’s journey in each of them is two days and a third, so that is twenty-eight mansions, then it is hidden for two nights, and the sun’s journey in each of them is a month.
85:2: And His statement: And the Promised Day, God Almighty says: And I swear by the day that I promised My servants, to decide the judgment between them, and that is the Day of Resurrection. The people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about this, and the report came from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Who said that? Abu Kurayb told us: Ibn Numayr and Ishaq al-Razi told us, on the authority of Musa ibn Ubaydah, on the authority of Ayoub ibn Khalid, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Rafi’, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The promised day is the Day of Resurrection.” He said: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Musa bin Ubaidah, on the authority of Ayoub bin Khalid, on the authority of Abdullah bin Rafi’, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, the same. Yaqub told us, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said: Yunus told us, he said: Ammar told me, he said: Abu Hurayrah said: The promised day is the Day of Resurrection. Yunus said: And so did Al-Hasan. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And the Promised Day means: the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, and the promised day, he said: the Resurrection. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said: And the Promised Day is the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Yunus ibn Ubayd, on the authority of Ammar ibn Abi Ammar, a client of the Banu Hashim, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah: And the Promised Day means the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Musa bin Ubaidah, on the authority of Ayoub bin Khalid, on the authority of Abdullah bin Rafi’, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: The promised day is the Day of Resurrection. Muhammad ibn Awf told us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Ayyash told us, he said: My father told me, he said: Damdam ibn Zur’ah told me, on the authority of Sharh ibn Ubayd, on the authority of Abu Malik al-Ash’ari, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The promised day is the Day of Resurrection.”
85:3: And his saying: And a witness and what is witnessed: The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of that. Some of them said: The meaning of that is: And I swear by a witness. They said: And it is Friday. And what is witnessed. They said: And it is the Day of Arafah. Who said that? Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said: Yunus told us, he said: Ammar told me, he said: Abu Hurayrah said, the witness: Friday, and the witnessed: the Day of Arafah. Yunus said: And this is what Al-Hasan said. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Muhammad Ibn Ja`far told us, he said: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, he said: I heard Haritha Ibn Mudrib narrating on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, that he said regarding this verse, And a witness and a witnessed, he said: Friday and the Day of Arafah. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And a witness and what is witnessed. He said: The witness is Friday, and what is witnessed is the Day of Arafah. It is also said: The witness is the human being, and what is witnessed is the Day of Resurrection. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And a witness and a witnessed: two great days of the days of this world. We were told that the witness is Friday, and the witnessed is the Day of Arafah. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: A witness and a witnessed. He said: The witness is Friday, and the witnessed is the Day of Arafah. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Harith, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him: And a witness and one witnessed. He said: The witness is Friday, and the one witnessed is the Day of Arafah. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his statement, and a witness is Friday, and and witnessed is the Day of Arafah. Abu Kurayb told us: Waki` told us, on the authority of Musa bin Ubaydah, on the authority of Ayoub bin Khalid, on the authority of Abdullah bin Rafi`, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘And the witness is Friday, and the witnessed is the Day of Arafah.’” Abu Kurayb told us: Ibn Numayr and Ishaq al-Razi told us, on the authority of Musa ibn Ubaydah, on the authority of Ayoub ibn Khalid, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Rafi’, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘The witnessed day is the Day of Arafah, and the witness is Friday.’” Sahl bin Musa told us: Ibn Abi Fadik told us, on the authority of Ibn Harmalah, on the authority of Saeed, that he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The master of days is Friday, and it is the witness, and the witnessed is the Day of Arafah.” Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Musa ibn Ubaydah, on the authority of Ayoub ibn Khalid, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Rafi’, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The witnessed day is the Day of Arafah, and the witness is Friday. In it is an hour in which no believer finds it and supplicates to God for good except that He answers him, and no one seeks refuge from evil except that He protects him. Muhammad ibn Awf told me, he said: Muhammad ibn Ismail told us, he said: My father told me, he said: Damdam ibn Zur’ah told me, on the authority of Shureih ibn Ubayd, on the authority of Abu Malik al-Ash’ari, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘The witness is on Friday, and the witnessed is on the Day of Arafah. Friday is God’s choice for us.’” Saeed bin Al-Rabi’ Al-Razi told me, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Harmalah, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, he said: The master of days is Friday, and it is a witness. Others said: The witness is Muhammad, and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection. Who said that? Abu Kurayb told us: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Ali bin Zaid, on the authority of Yusuf al-Makki, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The witness is Muhammad, and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection. Then he recited: That is a Day when mankind will be gathered together, and that is a witnessed Day (Hud 11:103). Ibn Humayd narrated: Jarir narrated from Mughirah from Shubak who said: A man asked Al-Hasan ibn Ali about and a witness and what is witnessed. He said: Did you ask anyone before me? He said: Yes, I asked Umar and Ibn Al-Zubayr, and they said: The Day of Sacrifice and Friday. He said: No, but the witness is Muhammad. Then he recited: How will it be when We bring from every nation a witness and We bring you, [O Muhammad], as a witness over these? (An-Nisa’: 41), and what is witnessed is the Day of Resurrection. Then he recited: That is a Day when mankind will be gathered together, and that is a witnessed Day. (Hud
85:4: And his saying: He killed the people of the trench, means: He cursed the people of the trench. Some of them used to say: The meaning of his saying He killed the people of the trench is report from God about the fire that it killed them. Scholars have differed about who the People of the Trench were. Some of them said: They were people of the Book from the remnants of the Magians. Who said that? Ibn Humayd narrated: Yaqub al-Qummi narrated from Ja'far from Ibn Abza, who said: When the Muhajirun returned from one of their military expeditions, they heard the report of the death of Umar ibn al-Khattab may God be pleased with him. Some of them said to one another: What rulings apply to the Magians, since they are not People of the Book, and they are not from the polytheists of the Arabs? Ali ibn Abi Talib may God be pleased with him said: They were People of the Book, and wine was made lawful for them. One of their kings drank it until he became intoxicated. He grabbed his sister and had intercourse with her. When the intoxication had gone away, he said to her: Woe to you! What is the way out of this trial that you have been afflicted with? She said: Address the people and say: O people, God has permitted the marriage of sisters. So he stood up and delivered a sermon and said: O people, God has permitted the marriage of sisters. The people said: We disavow this statement before God. No prophet brought it to us, nor did we find it in the Book of God. So he returned to her, regretful, and said to her: Woe to you! The people refused to acknowledge that, so she said: Strike them. So he did, and he struck them with whips, but they refused to acknowledge. So he returned to her regretting it and said: They refused to acknowledge. So she said: Propose to them, and if they refuse, then draw the sword on them. So he did, but the people refused. So he said to her: The people have refused. So he said: “Take the trench for them, then show her the people of your kingdom. Whoever acknowledges, otherwise throw him into the fire.” So he did, then he showed her the people of his kingdom. Whoever among them did not acknowledge, he threw him into the fire. So God revealed about them: The companions of the trench were killed, * The fire fueled until: That they believe in God, the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy. “Indeed, those who persecuted the believing men and believing women - they burned them - and then did not repent. For them is the punishment of Hell, and for them is the punishment of the Burning Fire.” And since that time they have not ceased to consider it permissible to marry sisters, daughters, and mothers. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, The Companions of the Trench were killed, he said: He told us that Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, used to say: They are people in the plains of Yemen, and its believers and disbelievers fought, so its believers were victorious over its disbelievers. Then they fought a second time, so its believers were victorious over its disbelievers. Then some of them took a covenant and an oath from each other that they would not betray each other, but the disbelievers betrayed them and seized them. Then a man from among the believers said to them: Do you want something good? Light a fire and expose us to it. Whoever follows your religion, that is what you desire, and whoever does not, will rush into the fire, so you will be relieved of him. He said: So they lit a fire and exposed them to it, and their leaders began to rush into it. Then an old woman remained among them as if she had turned back, so a child in her lap said to her: O mother, go on and do not act hypocritically. God has related to you their story and their tale. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, The companions of the trench were killed, he said: He means the killers who killed them on the day they were killed. Muhammad ibn Sa`d told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me: On the authority of his father: On the authority of Ibn `Abbas: The companions of the trench were killed, * The fueled fire. He said: They were people from the Children of Israel. They dug a trench in the ground, then lit a fire in it, then made men and women stand by that trench and parade them over it, and they claimed that it was Daniel and his companions. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, The companions of the trench were killed, he said: There were cracks in the ground in Najran, in which people were tortured. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement, The Companions of the Trench were killed, that they claim that the Companions of the Trench from the Children of Israel took men and women, dug a trench for themselves, then lit fires in it, and made the believers stand over it. They said: You disbelieve or we will throw you into the fire. Muhammad ibn Muammar told me: Harami ibn Ammar told me: Hammad ibn Salamah told us: Thabit al-Banani told us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Suhaib, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Among those who came before you, there was a king who had a magician. The magician came to the king and said: ‘I have grown old and my time is near, so give me a boy to teach me magic.’ So he gave him a boy to teach him magic. The boy would go frequently to the magician, and between the magician and the king was a monk. When the boy passed by the monk, he would sit beside him and listen to his speech, and he would be impressed by his speech. When the boy came to the magician, he would beat him and say: ‘What held you back?’ And when he came to his family, he would sit with the monk listening to his speech. When he returned to his family, they would beat him and say: ‘What held you back?’ So he complained about that to the monk, and the monk said to him: ‘If the magician says to you: What held you back?’ say: My family held me back. And if your family says: What held you back?’ say: The magician held me back.’” While he was like that, he passed by a road and saw a huge beast in the road, blocking the people and not letting them pass. The boy said, Now I know whether the matter of the magician is more pleasing to God than the matter of the monk. He took a stone and said, O God, if the matter of the monk is more beloved to You than the matter of the magician, then I will throw this stone with my stone and it will kill him and the people will pass by. So he threw it and killed it, and the people passed by. report of that reached the monk. The boy came to him and the monk said to the boy, You are better than me, and if you are tested, do not guide me to it. The boy cured the blind, the leper, and all other ailments. The king had a companion, and he became blind. It was said to him, There is a boy here who cures the blind, the leper, and all other ailments, if only you would come to him! He said: So he made him gifts. He said: Then he came to him and said: O boy, if you cure me, then all these gifts are yours. He said: I am not a doctor who can cure you, but God cures. If you believe, I will pray to God to heal you. The blind man believed, so he prayed to God and God healed him. The blind man sat before the king as he usually sits, and the king said to him: Were you not blind? He said: Yes. He said: Who healed you? He said: My Lord. He said: Do you have a Lord other than me? He said: Yes, my Lord and your Lord is God. He said: So he seized him with torment and said: Show me who taught you this. He said: So he showed me the boy. He called the boy and said: Abandon your religion. The boy refused. He said: So he seized him with torment. He said: So he showed me the monk. He took the monk and said: Abandon your religion. He refused. He said: So he placed the saw on his head and tore him apart until it reached the ground. He said: Then he took the blind man and said: Either you return or I will kill you. He said: The blind man refused. He placed the saw on his head and tore him apart until it reached the ground. Then he said to the boy: Either you return or I will kill you. He refused. He said: So he said: Take him until you reach the top of the mountain. If he returns, well and good, otherwise roll him down. When they reached the top of the mountain with him, they fell and all of them died. The boy came groping around until he entered upon the king. He said: Where are your companions? He said: God will suffice me against them. He said: Then take him and carry him in a boat and take him to the middle of the sea. If he renounces his religion, well and good, otherwise drown him. He said: So they took him, and when they took him to the middle of the sea, the rabbi said: O God, suffice me against them. So the ship capsized with them, and the boy came groping around until he entered upon the king. The king said: Where are your companions? He said, Leave God alone and He will suffice me against them. He said, I will kill you. He said, You will not kill me until you do what I command you. The boy said to the king, Gather the people in one place, then crucify me, then take an arrow from my quiver and shoot me and say, ‘In the name of the Lord of the boy,’ for you will kill me. So he gathered the people in one place, crucified him, took an arrow from his quiver, put it in the bow, then shot and said, In the name of the Lord of the boy. The arrow hit the boy’s temple. He placed his hand like this on his temple, and the boy died. The people said, We believe in the Lord of the boy. They said to the king, “What have you done? What you feared has happened. The people have believed.” So he ordered the mouths of the alleys to be taken, and a ditch to be dug and a fire to be set in it, and he seized them and said, If they return, then throw them into the fire. So they threw them into the fire. Then a woman came with her child. When she went to rush in, she felt the heat of the fire, so she retreated. Her son said to her: Oh mother, go ahead, for you are right. So she plunged into the fire. Others said: Rather, those who were burned by the fire were the infidels who tempted the believers. Who said that? It was narrated on the authority of Ammar, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ar-Rabi’ bin Anas, who said: The People of the Trench were a group of believers who had isolated themselves from people during the period of stagnation. A tyrant from among the idol worshippers sent to them and offered them to enter his religion, but they refused. So he dug a trench and lit a fire in it, then gave them the choice between entering his religion and being thrown into the fire. They chose to be thrown into the fire rather than abandon their religion, so they were thrown into the fire. God saved the believers who were thrown into the fire from the burning by taking their souls before the fire touched them. The fire came out to the unbelievers on the edge of the trench and burned them. This is what God says: For them is the punishment of Hell in the Hereafter, And for them is the punishment of the Burning Fire in this world. There is a difference of opinion about the place of the answer to the oath in His saying, And the heaven with its mansions. Some of them said: Its answer is, Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is severe. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: The oath was made here, Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is severe. Some of the grammarians of Basra said: The place of her oath, and God knows best, is on the killing of the People of the Trench. He omitted the lam, as he said, And the sun and its brightness (Ash-Shams 42:1), He has certainly succeeded who purifies it (Ash-Shams 42:9), meaning, God willing: He has certainly succeeded who purifies it. So he omitted the lam, and if you like, you can say it is in the introduction, as if he said: The People of the Trench were killed, and the sky with its constellations. Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: It is said in interpretation: The answer to the oath in His statement killed is like the oath and the sun and its brightness (Ash-Shams: 1) in His statement he has succeeded (Ash-Shams: 9). This is in interpretation. They said: We did not find the Arabs leaving the oath without a lam that is used to begin with or la or ma. If that is the case, then it is as if it is one in which the answer is left out, then the place of the answer is resumed with the report, as is said: O human being, in many speeches. The first of the sayings on this matter that is most correct in my opinion is the saying of the one who said: The answer to the oath in this matter is abandoned and the report is renewed because the Arabs do not delete the sign of the answer to the oath from the speech when they answer it. The first of the two interpretations of his saying, He killed the companions of the trench, is a curse on the companions of the trench who threw the believing men and women into the trench. Rather, I said: This is the more correct of the two interpretations of the reason that we mentioned from al-Rabi’, which is that God informed us that they will have the punishment of burning along with the punishment of Hell. If they had not been burned in this world, His statement, And they will have the punishment of burning would not have had an understood meaning, with His informing us that they will have the punishment of Hell, because the punishment of Hell is the punishment of burning along with all other types of punishment in the Hereafter. And the trench is the hole dug in the earth.
85:5: And his saying: The fire with fuel, so his saying the fire refers to the trench, and for this reason it was lowered, and it was only permissible to refer it to it even though it was not it, because it was in it, so it was as if since it was in it, the speech was directed towards it in order to know those addressed by it with its meaning, and it was as if it was said: The companions of the fire with fuel were killed, and he means by his saying with fuel the one with abundant firewood, and that is if the waw is opened, as for fuel with the waw closed, it is the kindling.
85:6: God Almighty says: The fire with fuel, as these infidels are among the people of the trench, over it, meaning on the fire. So He said over it, and the meaning is that they are sitting on the edge of the trench, so it was said on the fire, and the meaning is: on the edge of the trench, so that the listeners would know its meaning. Qatada used to say about this: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, The fire with fuel, when they were sitting by it, meaning the believers. This interpretation, which Qatada interpreted according to the school of thought of those who said: The people of the trench were killed from among the people of faith. We have shown that the correct interpretation of this is different from this statement, the interpretation of which was directed by Qatada before.
85:7: And His saying: And they are witnesses to what they do to the believers means: present. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And they are witnesses to what they do to the believers, meaning the disbelievers.
85:8: And His statement: And they did not resent them for anything except that they believed in God, the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy. God Almighty says: And these disbelievers who tempted the believing men and women with the Fire did not find anything in them, nor did they do to them what they did for any reason except because they believed in God. And He said: except that they believed in God, because the meaning is except their belief in God, so therefore it is appropriate in its place that they believe, since belief is an attribute for them. The Exalted says: Severe in His vengeance upon whoever He took vengeance from. The Praiseworthy says: Praised for His kindness to His creation.
85:9: God Almighty says: He who has authority over the seven heavens and the earths and whatever is in them, And God is Witness over all things. God Almighty says: God is Witness over the actions of these infidels, the Companions of the Trench, against the believers whom they tempted, and over other actions of theirs and the actions of all His creation, and He will reward them accordingly.
85:10: And His statement: Those who have put to trial the believing men and believing women means: Those who have tested the believing men and believing women with God by torturing them and burning them with fire. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Indeed, those who persecuted the believing men and women: they burned the believing men and women. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Indeed, those who were tried he said: were tormented. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Indeed, those who persecuted the believing men and believing women, he said: They burned them with fire. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, Persecute the believing men and believing women, that he said: Burn them. Ibn Hamid told us: Yaqub told us, on the authority of Ja`far, on the authority of Ibn Abza: Those who persecuted the believing men and women burned them. And His statement: Then they did not repent, meaning: Then they did not repent from their disbelief and the actions they did to the believing men and women because of their belief in God. Then they will have the punishment of Hell in the Hereafter, and they will have the punishment of the Burning Fire in this world. It was also narrated on the authority of Ammar, who said: Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’: For them is the punishment of Hell in the Hereafter, and for them is the punishment of the Burning Fire in this world.
85:11: God Almighty says: Indeed, those who acknowledged the Oneness of God, and they are these people who were burned by the People of the Trench and others from the rest of the people of Oneness, and did righteous deeds meaning: and worked in obedience to God, and obeyed His command, and refrained from what He forbade them from, for them are gardens beneath which rivers flow meaning: for them in the Hereafter with God are orchards beneath which rivers flow, and wine, milk, and honey. That is the great attainment meaning: this that is for these believers in the Hereafter is the great triumph in what they asked for and sought through their belief in God in this world, and their work in what God commanded them to do in it and was pleased with from them.
85:12: And His statement: Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is severe. God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Indeed, the punishment of your Lord, O Muhammad, against those of His creation who are afflicted by Him - and His vengeance against those against whom He takes vengeance - is severe. It is a warning from God to the people of His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, that He will inflict upon them His punishment and vengeance, similar to what befell the People of the Trench for their disbelief in Him, their denial of His Messenger, and their temptation of the believing men and women among them.
85:13: The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of His statement, Indeed, it is He who originates and restores. Some of them said: The meaning of that is: God originated His creation, so He originates, meaning: He brings about His creation in the beginning, then He causes them to die, then He restores them to life after their death, as they were before their death. Who said that? It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, He begins and repeats, meaning: creation. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, He begins and repeats, he said: He begins creation when He creates it, and He repeats it on the Day of Resurrection. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: He is the One who begins the punishment and repeats it. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Indeed, it is He who begins and repeats. He said: He begins the punishment and repeats it. The first of the two interpretations of this, in my opinion, is the most correct, and most similar to the apparent meaning of what the revelation indicates, is the statement we mentioned on the authority of Ibn Abbas, which is that He begins the punishment for the people of disbelief in Him and repeats it, as He, the Most High, said: For them is the punishment of Hell, and for them is the punishment of the Burning Fire (al-Buruj 85:10) in this world. So He began that for them in this world, and He will repeat it for them in the Hereafter. I said: This is the more correct of the two interpretations, because God followed that with His statement, Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is severe. So the explanation of the meaning of the severity of His punishment that He had mentioned before it was more like the explanation of what was not mentioned. And what supports what we have said clearly is His statement, And He is the Forgiving, the Loving. So He explained that from the fact that what preceded it of His mention was His report of His punishment and the severity of His chastisement.
85:14: And His statement: And He is the Forgiving, the Loving. God Almighty says: He is the One who forgives whoever repents to Him for his sins, and He is the One who loves him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, The Forgiving, the Loving, meaning: the Beloved. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding God’s statement, The Forgiving, the Loving, he said: The Most Merciful.
85:15: And His saying: Possessor of the Glorious Throne means the Almighty says: Possessor of the Noble Throne. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, Possessor of the Majestic Throne, meaning: the Generous. The reciters differed in their reading of His statement, The Glorious. The majority of the reciters of Medina, Mecca, and Basra, and some of the Kufians, read it in the nominative case, in response to His statement, Possessor of the Throne, on the basis that it is an attribute of God, the Most High, mentioned. The majority of the Kufian reciters read it in the genitive case, on the basis that it is an attribute of the Throne. The correct thing to say about this, in our view, is that they are two well-known readings, so whichever one the reader recites, he is correct.
85:16: And His statement: He does what He wills means: He is the Forgiver of the sins of whomever He wills of His servants if they repent and return from them, and He punishes whoever persists in them and persists in them. Nothing prevents Him from doing what He wants to do, and nothing stands between Him and that, because He owns the kingdom of the heavens and the earth, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
85:17: And His statement: Has there reached you the report of the soldiers? God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Has there reached you, O Muhammad, the report of the soldiers who have gathered against God and His Messenger with their harm and their harm? He says: This has come to you and you know it, so be patient with the harm your people will cause you, and with the harm they have caused you, just as those of My messengers who gathered against them were patient, and do not let that deter you from conveying My message to them, just as those who were sent to these people were not deterred, for the outcome of those among them who do not believe in you and have faith in you is ruin and destruction, like the one who was among these soldiers.
85:18: Then He, the Most High, explained who the soldiers were, saying: Pharaoh and Thamud. He said: Pharaoh, so He was satisfied with mentioning him, since he was the leader of his army, from mentioning his army and his followers. The meaning of the speech is: Has there come to you the story of the soldiers, Pharaoh and his people and Thamud? He lowered Pharaoh in response to the soldiers, on the translation of them, and it was opened because it does not run and Thamud.
85:19: God Almighty says: What is the matter with these people who deny God’s threat? They have not received any report from the nations who denied God’s messengers before them, such as Pharaoh and his people, Thamud and their likes, nor from the punishments that God brought upon them because of their denial of the messengers. Rather, they deny God’s revelation and His sending down, giving preference to their whims and following the ways of their fathers.
85:20: God Almighty says: And God is behind them, encompassing their deeds, and examining them. Nothing of them is hidden from Him, and He will reward them for all of them.
85:21: And His saying: Rather, it is a glorious Qur’an, He, may His praise be glorified, says as a refutation of those who say that the Qur’an is poetry and rhyme: It is not so, rather it is a noble Qur’an. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Rather, it is a glorious Qur’an, meaning: a noble Qur’an. Abu Kurayb told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Ash’ath ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Ja’far, on the authority of Sa’id, regarding his statement, Rather, it is a glorious Qur’an, he said: Noble.
85:22: And His saying: In a Preserved Tablet, God Almighty says: It is the Qur’an, recorded in a Preserved Tablet. The reciters differed in their reading of His statement preserved. Those who read it from the people of Hijaz read it, Abu Ja`far al-Qari` and Ibn Kathir, and those who read it from the reciters of Kufa, `Asim, al-A`mash, Hamza, and al-Kisa`i, and from the Basrans, Abu `Amr read it as preserved in the accusative case, meaning that the tablet is the one described as preserved. If that is the case, then the interpretation of preserved tablet is an addition to it and a subtraction from it, from what God established in it. Ibn Muhaysin from the Meccans read it, and Nafi` from the Medinans read it as preserved in the nominative case, in response to the Qur’an, on the basis that it is from its description and attribute, and it is as if the meaning of that according to their reading is: Rather, it is a glorious Qur’an, preserved from change and alteration in a tablet. The correct statement regarding this, in our view, is that they are two well-known readings in the readings of the regions, and their meanings are correct. So whichever of the two readings the reader reads, he is correct. Since that is the case, then whichever of the two readings the reader reads, the interpretation of the reading he reads is as we have explained. Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said: Yahya told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid: On a tablet, he said: In the Mother of the Book. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: In a Preserved Tablet with God. Others said: It was said to be preserved because it was on Israfil’s forehead. Who said that? Amr bin Ali told us, he said: I heard Qara bin Sulaiman, he said: Harb bin Surayj told us, he said: Abdul Aziz bin Suhaib told us, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, regarding his statement, Rather, it is a glorious Qur’an, in a Preserved Tablet, he said: The Preserved Tablet that God mentioned, Rather, it is a glorious Qur’an, in a Preserved Tablet, is on the forehead of Israfil.
